A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same eight-task image-classification calibration study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix expansion.

before.justification: v1 reports original ECE, Brier-score, and balanced-accuracy experiments comparing calibration methods, training losses, foundation-model finetuning, and ensembles across eight tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical comparisons of ensemble sizes in Figures A.12–A.15.

M1.justification: The calibration procedures, loss variants, model families, OOD-exposure adaptations, and ensemble calibration rules are retained. Algorithms 1–2 receive equivalent notation edits; the added ensemble-size experiments do not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight classification tasks and use Textures for semantic OOD exposure. Entity30's added row in Table A.1 documents an already evaluated dataset. The new image examples and ensemble-size tests do not expand task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated calibrators, OOD variants, DAC combinations, and training-loss comparators are retained. The ensemble-size analysis uses existing comparison methods. Methods listed in the new literature-comparison table are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 supplements the three-member ensemble protocol with two- and five-member ensembles in Figures A.12–A.15. Appendix A.2 also corrects the documented ECE bin averages, without establishing that score computation changed or experiments were rerun. Newly supplied training hyperparameters are disclosures rather than demonstrated setting changes.

E4.justification: Figures A.12–A.15 add a focused sensitivity analysis testing whether ensemble benefits and calibration-order findings depend on ensemble size, using ECE and Brier scores across the retained datasets. Existing OOD-exposure, DAC, embedding-space, and model-size analyses remain.

E5.justification: The Friedman and Nemenyi testing procedures and significance reporting are retained from v1 Appendix A.5 in v2 Appendix A.7. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. Ensemble member counts are not repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: v2 adds ECE and Brier results for two- and five-member ensembles alongside the three-member comparisons. Section 4.3.1 reports benefits already with two members and limited further improvement from three to five. The original main results and significance findings are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 corrects the confidence and accuracy definitions within each ECE bin by adding the missing 1/|Bm| normalization factors. This repairs the written mathematical definition. No new theorem or proof is introduced; the algorithm-notation changes are equivalent.

C1.justification: The abstract and central practical recommendations remain substantively unchanged: ER+LS for raw probabilities, OOD exposure for single-model calibration, foundation-model finetuning, calibration before ensembling, and ID–shifted calibration tradeoffs. The ensemble-size evidence supports these retained contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3.2 extends the applicability of the pre-ensembling calibration recommendation to the tested sizes of two, three, and five members, whereas v1 examined three-member ensembles. The conclusion also explicitly discusses the image-classification scope and dependence of the guidelines on currently evaluated methods.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4 and Table A.3 substantially expand training documentation: Adam, batch size 32, dataset- and architecture-specific learning rates, epoch limits, and full foundation-model finetuning at 10^-5. Table A.1 additionally supplies previously omitted Entity30 split sizes. These fill significant reproducibility gaps without demonstrating changes to the original training runs.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.3/Table A.2 explicitly compares the study with eight prior studies across datasets, shifts, calibration methods, ensembling, and foundation models. References to Zhang et al. (2022), Gustafsson et al. (2023), and Jorge et al. (2023) are added. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main narrative structure are retained. Changes include short additions to the ensemble discussion and conclusion, new appendix subsections, revised cross-references, notation cleanup, and updated author/publication information.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual material with dataset-example panels A.1–A.2, literature and training tables A.2–A.3, and ensemble-size plot grids A.12–A.15. Existing displays are resized, relocated, or renumbered, Table A.1 gains an Entity30 row, and Figure 4 relabels its vertical axes from OOD to SHIFTED.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through the training specifications and Entity30 split details, repairs the ECE definition, and strengthens ensemble guidance with size-sensitivity evidence. The central empirical findings remain stable. A new ambiguity remains: Appendix A.4 says all models used standard cross-entropy despite the retained five-loss comparison in Section 3.3. The additions nevertheless support a limited net improvement in clarity and evidential support.
